findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing `?` and `:website_name` is not marked as an untrusted attribute
findings.body: `ActiveModel::Serializer` expects conditional inclusion methods to end with `?` (`include_website_name?`), so `def include_website_name` on line 153 is never called and `website_name` is always serialized into the JSON (even as `nil` when `website` is blank). Furthermore, `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that it is hidden for TL0 users when viewed by anonymous users (`scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), whereas `website_name` is not. As a result, a TL0 user's website domain/path is leaked to anonymous users via `website_name`. Adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and removing the manual `include_website_name` method, since `untrusted_attributes` defines `include_website_name?` automatically) fixes both issues.

findings.title: `" ." << website_host` mutates a string literal in place
findings.body: On line 149, `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses `String#<<`, which mutates the receiver string literal `"."` rather than allocating a new string with `+`. If `frozen_string_literal: true` is enabled this will raise a `FrozenError` / `RuntimeError` (`can't modify frozen String`), and in older Ruby versions where string literals are shared across calls in some contexts or if `website_host` were ever passed on the left-hand side, in-place mutation causes subtle bugs. Use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host` instead.

findings.title: `website_name` is not updated on the client after saving user preferences
findings.body: Previously, `websiteName` was a computed property on the controller observing `model.website`, so editing and saving `website` in user preferences immediately updated the displayed website name on the user profile. Now that `website_name` is computed on the server in `UserSerializer`, `User#save` (around line 210, where `self.set('bio_excerpt', data.user.bio_excerpt)` is updated from the PUT response) does not copy `data.user.website_name` back onto the model. After a user updates their website in preferences and navigates back to their profile without a full page reload, `model.website_name` will remain stale (or undefined if they previously had no website).
